method: Actual current mediation handler; model and reasoning overridden for this process; one generation, no retry.

input.dispute: Utilities split evenly three ways when one person is home all day and the other two are not
input.yourSide: I work from home so I'm here with the heating on while they're both out. I get why they think even splits are simplest, but I'm also not the one who set the thermostat to 22 in November. I'd pay a bigger share of heating if we split internet and water evenly.
input.theirSide: They say an even split is the only thing that doesn't turn into a monthly argument, and that once you start metering one thing you end up metering everything. One of them also pointed out I use less water since I shower at the gym.

response.understanding: Utilities are currently split equally three ways; no agreement to change that is described. You work from home with the heating on, but say you did not choose the 22°C setting. Being home may increase heating demand, but does not establish how much extra you cause or control. Your lower water use is also a relevant offset when assessing the overall split. As you understand it, your housemates prefer equal shares to avoid recurring arguments. Your willingness to pay more for heating is a conditional offer, not an obligation or accepted agreement. The unclear point is whether anyone actually wants to change the split, or whether you are exploring what would be fair.

way_forward.recommendation: First clarify whether anyone is requesting a different split. If nobody is, there is no need to introduce one. If someone is, discuss the whole utilities arrangement alongside who controls the heating temperature and schedule.
way_forward.reason: An equal split can reasonably prioritize simplicity and offset different kinds of use. A different split could also work, but charging you more solely because you are home overlooks thermostat decisions and your lower water use.
supporting_actions: If a change is wanted, present your offer as a package: a larger heating share with internet and water remaining equal. Agree any amount together rather than treating your presence as proof of a particular surcharge.
Agree a comfortable heating temperature and schedule so any payment discussion reflects shared decisions about consumption.

words_you_can_use.script: Are we actually looking to change the equal split, or keep it? I'd consider paying a bigger heating share if internet and water stayed equal, but I'd want us to agree the heating setting and schedule too—I didn't choose 22 degrees.
